```{r setup}
library(forestsearch)

if (utils::packageVersion("forestsearch") < "0.4.0") {

}
```

```{=html}
<style>
#quarto-document-content table.table { width: auto; margin-left: 0; }
#quarto-document-content table.table th,
#quarto-document-content table.table td { padding: 0.25rem 0.9rem; }
```

Forest search works the same way on every outcome family. Each candidate
subgroup receives the trial's own analysis — here a logistic regression for a
binary endpoint and a linear regression for a continuous one — and the
selection correction and the one-sided bounds act on that analysis's
treatment coefficient: the log odds ratio, or the mean difference. This
article runs the analyses of the AIDS Clinical Trials Group 175 trial in the
two papers.

- **Part 1 — León and Anderson (2026b), Supplementary Section S3.** Forest
  search on the binary endpoint (no CD4 improvement at week 20, analysed as an
  odds ratio) and on the continuous endpoint (the CD4 decline to week 20,
  analysed as a mean difference): the corrected estimates, the one-sided field
  and field-s bounds and the Bonferroni pair of its Table S16, and the
  declaration calibration of its Table S17.
- **Part 2 — León and Anderson (2026a), Table S3 (Supplementary Section S7).**
  The binary endpoint with three identifiers — forest search (FS), DINA and
  GRF — and the full bootstrap correction beside multiplier resampling. The
  multiplier correction runs at the paper's 5,000 draws; the bootstrap runs at
  a small number of replicates, to show the machinery and its cost.

Every endpoint is oriented so that the adverse direction is upward — an odds
ratio above one, or a positive mean difference, is harm — so one screen and one
pair of bounds serve both, with no change of sign at the point of reading. The
bounds are read by where they lie against the trial's own effect and against
clinically meaningful effect sizes, not as tests at the null. The article runs
in about six minutes; most of it is the five searches, which run on one core.

## The data

ACTG 175 randomized HIV-infected adults to four antiretroviral regimens. The
analyses compare zidovudine plus didanosine (ZDV + ddI, arm 1) with didanosine
alone (ddI, arm 3): 1,083 patients, every one of them with a week-20 CD4 count.
Twelve baseline covariates enter every search: age, days of prior
antiretroviral therapy, weight, Karnofsky score, baseline CD4 and CD8 counts,
and six binary indicators — haemophilia, homosexual activity, a history of
injecting drug use, race, sex and symptomatic status.

```{r data}
actg <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg$id    <- seq_len(nrow(actg))
actg$treat <- as.integer(actg$arms == 1L)           # 1 = ZDV + ddI, 0 = ddI
stopifnot(nrow(actg) == 1083, !anyNA(actg$cd420))   # every patient has a week-20 CD4 count

cont_vars   <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars    <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)

# Binary endpoint: 1 = no CD4 improvement at week 20, the adverse outcome.
# The binary covariates stay numeric 0/1; forest search treats them as categorical.
df_bin <- actg
df_bin$y_binary_neg <- as.integer(!(df_bin$cd420 > df_bin$cd40))
for (v in bin_vars) df_bin[[v]] <- as.numeric(df_bin[[v]])

# Continuous endpoint: the CD4 decline from baseline to week 20, positive = worse.
# The binary covariates are factors, as in the applied analysis this one follows.
df_cont <- actg
df_cont$y_decline <- df_cont$cd40 - df_cont$cd420
for (v in bin_vars) df_cont[[v]] <- as.factor(df_cont[[v]])

# The whole-trial effects, with Wald 95% intervals
wald <- function(fit, back = identity) {
  b <- coef(fit)[["treat"]]; se <- sqrt(vcov(fit)["treat", "treat"])
  back(b + c(0, -1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se)
}
whole_or <- wald(glm(y_binary_neg ~ treat, family = binomial, data = df_bin), exp)
whole_md <- wald(lm(y_decline ~ treat, data = df_cont))
c(patients = nrow(actg), ZDV_ddI = sum(actg$treat == 1), ddI = sum(actg$treat == 0),
  no_improvement = sum(df_bin$y_binary_neg))
cat(sprintf("Whole trial: odds ratio of no improvement %.3f (%.3f, %.3f)\n",
            whole_or[1], whole_or[2], whole_or[3]),
    sprintf("             mean difference in CD4 decline %.1f (%.1f, %.1f) cells per mm3\n",
            whole_md[1], whole_md[2], whole_md[3]), sep = "")
```

Over the trial as a whole the combination leaves fewer patients without CD4
improvement and spares about 28 cells per mm³ of CD4 decline. Every bound
below is read against these two effects.

## Part 1 — the analyses of León and Anderson (2026b)

### The specification

The binary search uses the settings of the breast cancer analysis in
`vignette("forestsearch")`, on the odds-ratio scale. The continuous search
follows an existing applied analysis of the same outcome, with the selection
rule as its one departure.

- **Candidates** are conjunctions of at most two covariate cuts (`maxk = 2`)
  with more than 60 patients (`n.min`); on the binary endpoint each arm must
  also hold ten patients without improvement (`d0.min`, `d1.min`), a minimum
  that does not apply to a continuous outcome. The binary search carries ten
  candidate cuts on baseline CD4 and on weight, the continuous search ten on
  each of the six continuous covariates (`conf.cont_jcuts`); the remaining
  covariates take the package's default cuts.
- **Thresholds.** On the binary endpoint the screening and per-split
  thresholds are both an odds ratio of one, the claim threshold. On the CD4
  scale they are 10 and 5 cells per mm³, well below the trial's own effect.
  The consistency level is $p^\star = 0.90$, with the rate evaluated in
  closed form (`consistency_method = "resample"`; `fs.splits` sizes only the
  random-splitting fallback).
- **The selection rule** is $\max_{\mathcal{A}} N(\varepsilon)$ at
  $\varepsilon = 0.20$: the largest admitted region whose effect is within 20%
  of the largest.
- **Inference** from 5,000 multiplier draws: the corrected (two-term)
  estimate with its two-sided infinitesimal-jackknife (IJ) interval, the
  one-sided field lower bound on $\beta(\hat H)$, the field-s upper bound on
  $\beta(\hat H^{c})$, and the Bonferroni pair, a joint 95% claim on both. The
  field's own Monte Carlo runs at 1,000 outer and 500 inner draws. The
  declaration field is kept for the calibration of the last section of this
  part.

```{r fit-bin}
#| message: false
#| results: hide
t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fit_bin <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df_bin,
  outcome.name = "y_binary_neg", event.name = "y_binary_neg", treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = confounders,
  is.RCT = TRUE, seedit = 8316951,
  outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR", adverse_outcome = TRUE,
  # the candidate family
  conf.cont_jcuts = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  n.min = 60, d0.min = 10, d1.min = 10, maxk = 2,
  # the identifier, its thresholds and the selection rule
  subgroup_method = "consistency", consistency_method = "resample",
  effect.threshold = 1.00, consistency.threshold = 1.00, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  stop_threshold = NULL,                      # evaluate every candidate; no early stop
  sg_focus = "effMaxSG", selection_rule = "neighborhood", effect_neighborhood = 0.20,
  # selection-adjusted inference
  mr_inference = TRUE,
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", draws = 5000L, include_complement = TRUE,
                           field_scale_complement = "selected", field_decompose = TRUE,
                           keep_declaration_field = TRUE,
                           declaration_c0 = c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85)),
  quiet = TRUE, parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"))
sec_bin <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
```

```{r fit-cont}
#| message: false
#| results: hide
t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fit_cont <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df_cont,
  outcome.name = "y_decline", treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = confounders,
  is.RCT = TRUE, seedit = 8316951,
  outcome_type = "continuous", effect_measure = "MD", adverse_outcome = TRUE,
  # the candidate family
  conf.cont_jcuts = list(age = 10, preanti = 10, wtkg = 10, karnof = 10, cd40 = 10, cd80 = 10),
  n.min = 60, maxk = 2,
  # the identifier, its thresholds (CD4 cells per mm3) and the selection rule
  consistency_method = "resample", fs.splits = 500,
  effect.threshold = 10, consistency.threshold = 5, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  sg_focus = "effMaxSG", selection_rule = "neighborhood", effect_neighborhood = 0.20,
  # selection-adjusted inference
  mr_inference = TRUE,
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", draws = 5000L, include_complement = TRUE,
                           field_scale_complement = "selected",
                           keep_declaration_field = TRUE,
                           declaration_c0 = c(-5, -10, -15)),
  quiet = TRUE, parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"))
sec_cont <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
```

```{r regions}
in_region <- function(fit, d) fit$df.est$treat.recommend[match(d$id, fit$df.est$id)] == 0
in_bin  <- in_region(fit_bin, df_bin)
in_cont <- in_region(fit_cont, df_cont)
# the regions in words, checked against the package's membership
stopifnot(identical(in_bin,  df_bin$wtkg > 86 & df_bin$cd40 > 380),
          identical(in_cont, df_cont$cd40 > 507 & as.character(df_cont$gender) == "1"))
for (x in list(list("Binary", fit_bin, in_bin, sec_bin),
               list("Continuous", fit_cont, in_cont, sec_cont))) {
  g <- x[[2]]$mr_inference
  cat(sprintf("%-10s %-32s N %d   fit %.0f s (multiplier stage %.1f s)\n",
              x[[1]], paste(x[[2]]$sg.harm, collapse = " & "), sum(x[[3]]), x[[4]],
              g$timing_seconds))
}
```

On the binary endpoint forest search returns the 72 patients weighing more than
86 kg with baseline CD4 above 380 cells per mm³; on the continuous endpoint, the
79 men with baseline CD4 above 507. The package writes a region as a
conjunction of the cut indicators it searched — `!{cd40 <= 380}` is "CD4 above
380" and `{gender}` is "male" — and the chunk above checks each against its
description in words. The two regions are selected on different endpoints of
the same patients and are not the same set; each leaves a complement of about
93% of the trial.

### The regions and their adjusted effects

Every number of Table S16 but the whole-trial row is in `fit$mr_inference`:
the unadjusted and corrected estimates and the selection bias in its top level,
the bounds in `$field`, and the complement's quantities in `$complement` and
`$field$complement`. The helper below reads them in the table's order, on the
outcome's own scale.

```{r s16-helper}
s16_column <- function(fit, d, y, digits, events) {
  g  <- fit$mr_inference; cc <- g$complement
  fb <- g$field; fc <- fb$complement; js <- fb$joint_s
  in_H <- in_region(fit, d)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(in_H), sum(in_H) == g$n_selected, sum(!in_H) == cc$n)
  f  <- function(x) sprintf("%.*f", digits, x)
  ci <- function(e, l, u) sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", f(e), f(l), f(u))
  n_ev <- function(sel) {
    n <- format(sum(sel), big.mark = ",")
    if (events) sprintf("%s (%d)", n, sum(d[[y]][sel])) else n
  }
  c(n_ev(rep(TRUE, nrow(d))),
    paste(fit$sg.harm, collapse = " & "),
    n_ev(in_H),
    ci(g$naive$est, g$naive$lower, g$naive$upper),
    ci(g$debiased$est, g$debiased$lower, g$debiased$upper),
    f(fb$lower_1s),
    n_ev(!in_H),
    ci(cc$naive$est, cc$naive$lower, cc$naive$upper),
    ci(cc$debiased$est, cc$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$upper),
    f(fc$upper_1s_s),
    sprintf("%s / %s", f(js$bonf_lower_H), f(js$bonf_upper_Hc)),
    f(g$selection_bias),
    format(g$n_family, big.mark = ","))
}
s16_rows <- c("Whole trial N (events)", "Whole-trial estimate, 95% CI", "Region", "N (events)",
              "Unadjusted, 95% CI", "Corrected (two-term), IJ interval", "Field, lower bound",
              "Complement N (events)", "Unadjusted, 95% CI", "Corrected (two-term), IJ interval",
              "Field-s, upper bound", "Bonferroni pair", "Selection bias", "Re-selection family")
col_bin  <- s16_column(fit_bin,  df_bin,  "y_binary_neg", digits = 3, events = TRUE)
col_cont <- s16_column(fit_cont, df_cont, "y_decline",    digits = 1, events = FALSE)
s16 <- data.frame(
  row = s16_rows,
  binary = c(col_bin[1], sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", whole_or[1], whole_or[2], whole_or[3]),
             col_bin[-1]),
  continuous = c(col_cont[1], sprintf("%.1f (%.1f, %.1f)", whole_md[1], whole_md[2], whole_md[3]),
                 col_cont[-1]))
knitr::kable(s16, col.names = c("", "Binary, OR", "Continuous, MD (CD4 cells)"),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
             caption = paste("This article's run. Corrected rows carry the two-term estimate with its",
                             "two-sided IJ interval; the field and field-s rows are one-sided bounds at",
                             "nominal 0.95; the Bonferroni pair holds both at joint 0.95. Selection bias",
                             "is on the log scale for the odds ratio and in CD4 cells for the mean difference."))
```

The two ACTG 175 columns of Table S16 of León and Anderson (2026b), as
published:

```{r s16-published}
s16_published <- data.frame(
  row = s16_rows,
  binary = c("1,083 (430)", "0.665 (0.520, 0.850)", "weight > 86 kg and CD4 > 380", "72 (37)",
             "3.584 (1.315, 9.774)", "1.773 (0.604, 5.206)", "0.686", "1,011 (393)",
             "0.587 (0.454, 0.759)", "0.620 (0.372, 1.033)", "0.786", "0.597 / 0.817",
             "0.704", "2,794"),
  continuous = c("1,083", "-27.6 (-43.1, -12.1)", "CD4 > 507 and male", "79",
                 "71.1 (-5.1, 147.3)", "22.1 (-77.5, 121.6)", "-38.3", "1,004",
                 "-36.2 (-51.4, -20.9)", "-32.7 (-62.2, -3.2)", "-17.6", "-51.2 / -15.8",
                 "47.9", "4,935"))
knitr::kable(s16_published, col.names = c("", "Binary, OR", "Continuous, MD (CD4 cells)"),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
             caption = "Table S16 of León and Anderson (2026b), the two ACTG 175 columns, as published.")
```

The run reproduces every number of the published columns; only the region is
written differently, in the package's notation.

```{r s16-values}
#| echo: false
gb <- fit_bin$mr_inference; gm <- fit_cont$mr_inference
r3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x); r1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
```

- **The binary endpoint.** In the region the unadjusted odds ratio is
  `r r3(gb$naive$est)`. The correction, over a selection bias of
  `r r3(gb$selection_bias)` on the log scale, brings it to
  `r r3(gb$debiased$est)`: much attenuated, suggestive of limited benefit of
  the combination in these patients, but with a field lower bound of
  `r r3(gb$field$lower_1s)`, below one, a benefit cannot be ruled out. Outside
  the region the corrected odds ratio, `r r3(gb$complement$debiased$est)`,
  favours the combination at least as much as the trial's own
  `r r3(whole_or[1])`, with a field-s upper bound of
  `r r3(gb$field$complement$upper_1s_s)`.
- **The continuous endpoint** has the same shape on the additive scale. The
  unadjusted mean difference in the region is `r r1(gm$naive$est)` cells; the
  correction removes `r r1(gm$selection_bias)` cells of selection bias and
  leaves `r r1(gm$debiased$est)` on the adverse side, with a field lower bound
  of `r r1(gm$field$lower_1s)`, below zero. Outside the region the corrected
  estimate, `r r1(gm$complement$debiased$est)`, again favours the
  combination, with a field-s upper bound of
  `r r1(gm$field$complement$upper_1s_s)` cells.
- **The common reading.** An unadjusted analysis of either region would
  report a substantial adverse effect. After correction each region's estimate
  is much attenuated, with a lower bound that does not rule out a benefit; in
  each case the patients outside the region — the part of the trial the search
  was not looking at — show a benefit of the combination.

### Declaration at a protected level

Forest search declared both regions at the default screen, $p^\star = 0.90$.
Section 4 of León and Anderson (2026b) asks whether a screen calibrated to
protect a clinically meaningful uniform benefit would have declared them: an
odds ratio of 0.75 on the binary endpoint, and ten cells per mm³ of CD4 decline
spared on the continuous one, each on a grid around it, at a family-wise level
$\alpha = 0.10$. `fs_declaration_calibration()` reads the answer from the
multiplier draws each fit already made; nothing is redrawn (see
`vignette("forestsearch")` for the construction).

```{r declaration}
s17_column <- function(fit, c0_grid, c0_primary, fmt_c0) {
  cal    <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10, c0 = c0_grid)
  cal_c2 <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10)   # c0 = NULL: the claim threshold
  stopifnot(identical(cal$c0$source, "capture"))            # read from the fit's own draws
  fld <- fit$mr_inference$declaration_field
  T_H <- cal$T_hat[[fld$family_id[fld$meta$selected_index]]]
  tb  <- cal$c0$table; i <- which(tb$c0 == c0_primary)
  admits_none <- all(lengths(cal$c0$admitted_calibrated) == 0) &&
    length(cal_c2$admitted_calibrated) == 0
  c(fit$mr_inference$n_selected,
    sprintf("%.3f / %.3f", T_H, max(cal$T_hat, na.rm = TRUE)),
    fmt_c0(c0_primary),
    sprintf("%.3f", tb$kappa_hat[i]),
    sprintf("%.3f", 2 * pnorm(tb$kappa_hat[i]) - 1),
    sprintf("%.3f", tb$fw_size[i]),
    sprintf("%.3f", cal_c2$kappa_hat),
    sprintf("%.3f", cal_c2$fw_size),
    if (admits_none) "admits nothing" else "admits a candidate")
}
s17_rows <- c("Region declared at the default level, N", "T of the region / largest T in the family",
              "Primary protected level c0", "Calibrated cutoff, kappa-hat(c0)",
              "Implied level, 2 Phi(kappa-hat) - 1",
              "Diagnostic at the default screen's cutoff", "Calibrated cutoff at the claim threshold",
              "Diagnostic at the claim threshold", "Calibrated rule, every c0 and the claim threshold")
s17 <- data.frame(
  row = s17_rows,
  binary = s17_column(fit_bin, c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85), 0.75, function(x) sprintf("OR %.2f", x)),
  continuous = s17_column(fit_cont, c(-5, -10, -15), -10, function(x) sprintf("MD %g cells", x)))
knitr::kable(s17, col.names = c("", "Binary, odds ratio", "Continuous, mean difference"),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
             caption = paste("This article's run, at alpha = 0.10. The diagnostic is the family-wise size",
                             "of the p* = 0.90 screen as executed, were every candidate to carry a uniform",
                             "benefit of c0; at the claim threshold it is a boundary size."))
```

The two ACTG 175 columns of Table S17 of León and Anderson (2026b), as
published:

```{r s17-published}
s17_published <- data.frame(
  row = s17_rows,
  binary = c("72", "2.494 / 2.494", "OR 0.75", "2.889", "0.996", "0.838", "3.611", "0.989",
             "admits nothing"),
  continuous = c("79", "1.701 / 2.043", "MD -10 cells", "2.952", "0.997", "0.909", "3.625", "0.997",
                 "admits nothing"))
knitr::kable(s17_published, col.names = c("", "Binary, odds ratio", "Continuous, mean difference"),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
             caption = "Table S17 of León and Anderson (2026b), the two ACTG 175 columns, as published.")
```

In both analyses the returned region's statistic sits below the calibrated
cutoff, and so does the largest statistic in its family, so the calibrated
screen admits no candidate — at every protected level on the grid and at the
claim threshold. Had the combination benefited every patient by the protected
amount, the default screen would still have returned a harm subgroup in
`r s17$binary[6]` (binary) and `r s17$continuous[6]` (continuous) of such
trials, on these families and this covariate design. The implied levels,
`r s17$binary[5]` and `r s17$continuous[5]`, say what the calibration asks of
these trials: a screen far tighter than the default, which is what a large
overlapping family costs once the protection is placed at a clinically
meaningful benefit.

## Part 2 — Table S3 of León and Anderson (2026a)

### The settings

The forest-search call is the one in the paper's own document: Part 1's
search with the neighbourhood at $\varepsilon = 0.10$, the value that paper
sets, and the package's default early stop in the consistency stage. Two
further identifiers stand beside it. DINA and GRF propose their candidates from a
surface fitted to the outcome, and their qualifying regions are re-ranked on
the odds ratio (`*_select_statistic = "effect"`): DINA with a two-fold
cross-fitted surface and a floor of an odds ratio of one, GRF on the frontier
of its covariate grid at depth 2 with a floor of zero on its doubly-robust
risk-difference score. Each fit carries multiplier resampling at 5,000 draws,
reported as the two-term corrected estimate with its two-sided IJ interval.

```{r fit-s3-fs}
#| message: false
#| results: hide
t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fit_s3_fs <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df_bin,
  outcome.name = "y_binary_neg", event.name = "y_binary_neg", treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = confounders,
  is.RCT = TRUE, seedit = 8316951,
  outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR", adverse_outcome = TRUE,
  conf.cont_jcuts = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  n.min = 60, d0.min = 10, d1.min = 10, maxk = 2,
  subgroup_method = "consistency", consistency_method = "resample", fs.splits = 500,
  effect.threshold = 1.0, consistency.threshold = 1.0, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  sg_focus = "effMaxSG", selection_rule = "neighborhood", effect_neighborhood = 0.10,
  mr_inference = TRUE, mr_inference_args = list(draws = 5000L),
  quiet = TRUE, parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"))
sec_s3_fs <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
```

```{r fit-s3-dina}
#| message: false
#| results: hide
t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fit_s3_dina <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df_bin,
  outcome.name = "y_binary_neg", event.name = "y_binary_neg", treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = confounders,
  is.RCT = TRUE, seedit = 8316951,
  outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR", adverse_outcome = TRUE,
  subgroup_method = "dina", dina_select_statistic = "effect",
  dina_args = list(seed = 8316951L, n_folds = 2L),
  effect.threshold = 1.0, n.min = 60,
  sg_focus = "effMaxSG", selection_rule = "neighborhood", effect_neighborhood = 0.10,
  mr_inference = TRUE, mr_inference_args = list(draws = 5000L),
  quiet = TRUE, parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"))
sec_s3_dina <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
```

```{r fit-s3-grf}
#| message: false
#| results: hide
t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fit_s3_grf <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df_bin,
  outcome.name = "y_binary_neg", event.name = "y_binary_neg", treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = confounders,
  is.RCT = TRUE, seedit = 8316951,
  outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR", adverse_outcome = TRUE,
  subgroup_method = "grf", grf_selection = "frontier", grf_select_statistic = "effect",
  grf_depth = 2L, dmin.grf = 0.0, n.min = 60,
  sg_focus = "effMaxSG", selection_rule = "neighborhood", effect_neighborhood = 0.10,
  mr_inference = TRUE, mr_inference_args = list(draws = 5000L),
  quiet = TRUE, parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"))
sec_s3_grf <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
```

```{r s3-selected}
fits_s3 <- list(FS = fit_s3_fs, DINA = fit_s3_dina, GRF = fit_s3_grf)
secs_s3 <- c(FS = sec_s3_fs, DINA = sec_s3_dina, GRF = sec_s3_grf)
stopifnot(identical(in_region(fit_s3_fs, df_bin), in_bin))   # the region of Part 1
for (m in names(fits_s3)) {
  gm <- fits_s3[[m]]$mr_inference
  cat(sprintf("%-4s %-38s N %3d   fit %5.1f s (multiplier stage %4.1f s)   family %d\n",
              m, paste(fits_s3[[m]]$sg.harm, collapse = " & "), gm$n_selected, secs_s3[[m]],
              gm$timing_seconds, gm$n_family))
}
agree <- in_region(fit_s3_fs, df_bin) == in_region(fit_s3_grf, df_bin)
cat(sprintf("FS and GRF classify %d of %d patients alike\n", sum(agree), length(agree)))
```

Forest search returns Part 1's region: on this frontier the largest admitted
region is also the one with the largest odds ratio, so $\varepsilon$ does not
decide the selection, though the multiplier draws re-apply the rule as each fit
specifies it and the correction moves slightly. DINA returns the 98 patients
with at least 849 days of prior antiretroviral therapy and baseline CD4 of at
least 338; GRF the 95 weighing more than 84.4 kg with baseline CD4 above 368, a
region close to forest search's but not the same.

### The full bootstrap

`forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()` draws a nonparametric bootstrap sample and
re-runs the identifier on it — the whole search, the screen and the selection,
with the front-end surfaces refitted for DINA and GRF — and corrects the
observed estimate by the bootstrap estimate of its selection bias (León et al.
2024). Multiplier resampling is not run inside the replicates
(`mr_in_replicates = FALSE`, the default), so each replicate costs one search.

The paper used B = 1,000. Here B is small, to show the implementation and its
cost: the point estimates serve as an illustration, the intervals do not — the
finite-B variance needs B in the hundreds — so the bootstrap column below
carries the point estimate only. Replicates are independent and run through
the **future** framework; this article uses at most two workers, and for a real
run `n_workers` should be the cores you have.

```{r bootstrap}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
n_workers <- min(2L, future::availableCores())   # set to your cores for a real run
boot_plan <- if (n_workers > 1L) list(plan = "multisession", workers = n_workers) else
  list(plan = "sequential")
B <- c(FS = 25L, DINA = 25L, GRF = 10L)
boots <- list(); boot_secs <- c()
for (m in names(fits_s3)) {
  t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  boots[[m]] <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
    fs.est = fits_s3[[m]], nb_boots = B[[m]], seed = 8316951L,
    mr_in_replicates = FALSE, parallel_args = boot_plan)
  boot_secs[m] <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
}
round(boot_secs, 1)
```

### Naive, bootstrap and multiplier side by side

```{r s3-columns}
three_columns <- function(method, fit, boot) {
  g <- fit$mr_inference; cc <- g$complement
  n_H <- g$n_selected; n_Hc <- cc$n
  f2 <- function(e, l, u) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", e, l, u)
  data.frame(
    method = method, region = c("H", "Hc"),
    n = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", c(n_H, n_Hc), round(100 * c(n_H, n_Hc) / (n_H + n_Hc))),
    naive = c(f2(g$naive$est, g$naive$lower, g$naive$upper),
              f2(cc$naive$est, cc$naive$lower, cc$naive$upper)),
    bootstrap = sprintf("%.2f", c(boot$H_estimates$H2, boot$Hc_estimates$H2)),
    multiplier = c(f2(g$debiased$est, g$debiased$lower, g$debiased$upper),
                   f2(cc$debiased$est, cc$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$upper)))
}
side_by_side <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits_s3), function(m)
  three_columns(m, fits_s3[[m]], boots[[m]])))
boot_label <- sprintf("Full bootstrap estimate (B = %d / %d / %d)",
                      B[["FS"]], B[["DINA"]], B[["GRF"]])
knitr::kable(side_by_side, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrr",
             col.names = c("Method", "SG", "n (%)", "Naive", boot_label, "Multiplier (5,000 draws)"),
             caption = paste("This article's run: odds ratios of no CD4 improvement with 95% intervals;",
                             "the bootstrap estimate at a small B, without an interval."))
```

Table S3 of León and Anderson (2026a), as published, with the full bootstrap at
B = 1,000:

```{r s3-published}
table_s3 <- data.frame(
  method = rep(c("FS", "DINA", "GRF"), each = 2), region = rep(c("H", "Hc"), 3),
  n = c("72 (7%)", "1011 (93%)", "98 (9%)", "985 (91%)", "95 (9%)", "988 (91%)"),
  naive = c("3.58 (1.31, 9.77)", "0.59 (0.45, 0.76)", "1.94 (0.84, 4.47)",
            "0.60 (0.46, 0.78)", "2.25 (0.97, 5.20)", "0.58 (0.45, 0.76)"),
  bootstrap = c("2.43 (0.80, 7.33)", "0.61 (0.41, 0.89)", "0.85 (0.23, 3.11)",
                "0.63 (0.40, 1.02)", "1.09 (0.40, 3.01)", "0.63 (0.38, 1.04)"),
  multiplier = c("1.79 (0.63, 5.08)", "0.62 (0.37, 1.03)", "0.95 (0.29, 3.10)",
                 "0.63 (0.38, 1.06)", "1.10 (0.43, 2.80)", "0.62 (0.37, 1.04)"))
knitr::kable(table_s3, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrr",
             col.names = c("Method", "SG", "n (%)", "Naive", "Full bootstrap (B = 1,000)",
                           "Multiplier"),
             caption = "Table S3 of León and Anderson (2026a), as published.")
```

```{r s3-values}
#| echo: false
r2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
gf <- fit_s3_fs$mr_inference
```

- **Naive and multiplier columns.** The regions, their sizes and the naive
  estimates are those of the published table, and so are the DINA and GRF
  multiplier rows. The published table was computed under forestsearch 0.2.0;
  under the current release the forest-search multiplier cells move in the
  third decimal, so the region's interval ends at `r r2(gf$debiased$upper)`
  where the table prints 5.08. DINA's and GRF's agree with the earlier release
  to every printed digit.
- **The bootstrap column** at this B illustrates the implementation. At
  B = 1,000 the paper finds the two corrections close for GRF (1.09 and 1.10),
  apart for forest search (2.43 and 1.79, both far below the naive 3.58), and
  both below one for DINA (0.85 and 0.95). DINA's and GRF's families are
  themselves regenerated by the bootstrap, so there the two routes answer
  different questions.
- **Reading, by location.** The forest-search region's corrected odds ratios,
  `r r2(gf$debiased$est)` by multiplier resampling and 2.43 by the paper's
  bootstrap, stay above one, at about half the naive `r r2(gf$naive$est)`;
  GRF's region corrects to marginally above one and DINA's to below one. In
  every case the complement's corrected odds ratio favours the combination.

### The cost of the two corrections

```{r cost}
cost <- data.frame(
  method = names(fits_s3),
  mr_seconds = sapply(fits_s3, function(f) f$mr_inference$timing_seconds),
  bootstrap_B = B[names(fits_s3)],
  bootstrap_seconds = boot_secs[names(fits_s3)])
cost$seconds_per_replicate <- cost$bootstrap_seconds / cost$bootstrap_B
cost$projected_B_1000 <- round(cost$seconds_per_replicate * 1000)
plan_label <- if (n_workers > 1L) sprintf("%d workers", n_workers) else "one process"
knitr::kable(cost, row.names = FALSE, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Method", "MR (s)", "B", "bootstrap (s)", "s per replicate",
                           "projected at B = 1,000 (s)"),
             caption = sprintf(paste(
               "Wall-clock timings from this run: the multiplier stage under the fits'",
               "sequential plan, the bootstrap on %s. The projection is linear in B",
               "at that worker count."), plan_label))
```

The multiplier correction is seconds; the bootstrap is minutes at the B its
intervals need. The MR column is the whole multiplier stage as each fit records
it (`timing_seconds`), here including the field bounds the current release
computes by default; the bootstrap column is the whole
`forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()` call on `r plan_label`. The document behind
Table S3 ran its B = 1,000 in 905 s (FS), 63 s (DINA) and 342 s (GRF) on 14
workers, under forestsearch 0.2.0 on another machine; those figures are not
comparable second for second with this run, and the order of magnitude between
the two routes is the point.

## Running at the papers' settings

Part 1 already runs at the settings of León and Anderson (2026b), the 5,000
multiplier draws and the field's 1,000 outer and 500 inner draws included. For
Part 2's bootstrap at the paper's size, set
`B <- c(FS = 1000L, DINA = 1000L, GRF = 1000L)` and `n_workers` to the cores
available, and use the cost table above to judge the wall-clock first.

## Where to go next

  data of León and Anderson (2026b), with the declaration calibration set out
  step by step.
- The [post-selection article](https://larry-leon.github.io/forestsearch/articles/survival-post-selection.html)
  is Part 2's comparison on the survival scale, Table S2 of León and Anderson
  (2026a), with the package's own bootstrap summaries and the diagnostics of
  the multiplier correction.
- `?forestsearch` documents every argument, with examples for the binary and
  continuous paths; `?fs_declaration_calibration`,
  `?forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture`.
